text:
maria: quick thread  drafting follow-up RFC for the continuous batching scheduler - aiming for a unified small-request fastpath that doesn't fragment queues. want a short list of operational risks and interface boundaries.

kevin: high level  love the unified path idea. two quick risks: starvation from kv-pointer holding, and increased kernel-launch churn hurting throughput.

lina: agree. we should split responsibilities: scheduler decides admission + soft deadlines; runtime owns kv eviction and can signal pressure. define a minimal API:

```
// scheduler -> runtime
admit_request(id, window_hint_ms, priority)
// runtime -> scheduler
pressure_signal(kernel_launch_rate, kv_eviction_rate)
// runtime eviction hint
kv_eviction_hint(request_id, urgency)
```

maria: that API looks good. for preemption semantics i propose "soft-lease" where after lease expiry runtime can either pause preserving kv pointers (preferred) or evict and requeue as cold. requeue should lower priority with an age-boost to avoid starvation.

kevin: add a protected bit at admission if the admission probe sees kv_touch_count >= N. protected=true bypasses soft-lease. cheap to compute and avoids losing high-reuse requests.

lina: telemetry list: kernel_launch_rate, fastpath_concurrency, kv_touch_histogram, preempt_requeue_count, prefix_reuse_ratio, fastpath_p95/p99. also add an approximate cost metric: extra_kernel_launchs_per_minute * cost_per_launch. product will ask for unit-econ.

maria: rollout playbook draft: enable fastpath in canary with concurrency=1, run mixed synthetic load (short bursts + long tails) for 1h. rollback conditions: kernel_launch_rate > baseline*2 AND throughput drop > 10% OR prefix_reuse_ratio drop > 15%.

infra-bot: i can provision the feature flag and a dashboard. suggest flags: fastpath.unified.canary, fastpath.max_tokens, fastpath.adaptive_window=true. will create alerts for kernel_launch_rate > 2x baseline (5m) and preempt_requeue_count > threshold. :robot_face:

maria: one more tradeoff to record: fastpath reduces tail latency but can harm batching efficiency long term; include an adaptive knob that reduces fastpath tokens if runtime pressure_signal indicates sustained high launch rate. control loop should be simple and conservative.

kevin: for the RFC include a short pseudo-code of the control loop and the admission interface (header only). i'll review the control loop.

lina: i'll review the kv_eviction_hint behavior and streaming edge cases (clients expecting continuous output when requeued).

maria: thanks all. i'll draft and ping reviewers.
